goals.statement: U134 holds on main: with a Drawer open in the main workspace, the Rail and the Shelf compute `--sunken`, the pane and the Drawer `--ground`; no border is wider than 1 px or any colour but `--hairline`; only the Drawer has a `box-shadow` (`--shadow-drawer`); no `backdrop-filter` element contains another; and opening the Drawer does not change the Terminal's size (D8).
goals.observer: `u134_` tests in `apps/desktop/src/drawer/u134_surfaces.test.tsx` run on the task's main, plus an independent read of computed style on the rendered workspace in the browser harness (U26) with a Drawer open.

goals.statement: U135 holds on main: under each of `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, `prefers-contrast: more`, `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` alone, every Token takes its dark value in dark; `--grey` text computes as `--text` and `--hairline` 40% opaque under more contrast; no element has a `backdrop-filter` under reduced transparency; every duration except the instant changes is `0s` under reduced motion; text keeps 4.5:1 and every Glyph tone and focus ring 3:1 against its own ground; D1 to D9 hold in each, and D10 at 700 by 800.
goals.observer: `u135_` tests in `apps/desktop/src/app/u135_schemes.test.tsx` run on the task's main, plus `window.__checks()` (U137) evaluated in the browser harness under each media setting and at 700x800.

goals.statement: In dark, the main workspace with a selected Terminal shows no light block: the pane's `--ground` (U134) extends through the Terminal, whose emulator background, foreground, cursor and selection are the dark values of `--ground`, `--text` and `--selected` (U59 read with U135's 'in dark every Token takes its dark value').
goals.observer: In the browser harness under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, the `.xterm-viewport` computed background and the emulator theme read back equal the dark `--ground`/`--text`/`--selected`; a Vitest check compares the emulator's dark theme fields to the dark column of `tokens.css`.

deliveries.title: U59 dark: specify the Terminal's dark theme so it follows the scheme
deliveries.body:
## Outcome
U59 says the emulator's background is `--ground`, its foreground and cursor `--text`, its selection the Rail's band, and its 16 ANSI colours "a light palette". `apps/desktop/src/terminal/theme.ts` hard-codes the light values, so since #349 turned dark on (U135) the selected Terminal stays a white block inside a dark pane (#349's body: "Not done: the Terminal's xterm theme is still the light palette"). `docs/design-system.md` directs "Light and dark". This delivery amends U59 in `scenarios/ui.md` so the Terminal follows the active scheme; implementation is a later Work Issue blocked by this one.

## Scope
`scenarios/ui.md` (U59 only). Specification only: no code under `apps/`.

## Acceptance
The amended U59 states, mechanically:
- In each scheme, the emulator's `background`, `cursorAccent` are the active scheme's `--ground`; `foreground` and `cursor` its `--text`; `selectionBackground` its `--selected`; a scheme change while a Terminal is open repaints it without a reload or losing scrollback.
- A dark ANSI palette of 16 colours, each at 4.5:1 or better as text on the dark `--ground`; a colour that cannot is named in the test with its measured ratio, none under 3:1; the light palette keeps its existing rule on the light `--ground`.
- Under `prefers-contrast: more`, the default foreground is `--text` (unchanged) and no ANSI colour falls below 4.5:1.
- A program that sets its own background is still drawn as it asks.
- Observers: Vitest compares each theme field to the matching column of `tokens.css` in light and dark and computes each ANSI colour's contrast in both; the browser harness (U26) reads `.xterm-viewport`'s computed background equal to the dark `--ground` under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.
- Test names: `u59_` (amended), and states its Owns: `apps/desktop/src/terminal/**` and its stylesheet.
Observer: an independent review of the specification PR checks each bullet above appears in U59 on its head, and that `just check` passes.

## Preserve
Every existing U59 clause for light; U101–U103 and U11–U14 Terminal behaviour; every existing test.

## Queue
Scenarios: U59
Specification: [scenarios/ui.md](https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/ui.md)
Key: U59-dark-spec
Priority: 50
Mode: specify
Provider: any

rules.content: **U59 the terminal blends with the app.** (amended clause) In each colour scheme the emulator's `background` and `cursorAccent` are that scheme's `--ground`, its `foreground` and `cursor` that scheme's `--text`, and its `selectionBackground` that scheme's `--selected`; when the scheme changes while a Terminal is open, the emulator repaints with the new values without a reload and keeps its scrollback. The 16 ANSI colours come from a light palette in light and a dark palette in dark, each reading at 4.5:1 or better as text on that scheme's `--ground` (U4's rule); a colour that cannot is named in the test with its measured ratio and scheme, and none is under 3:1. Observers: Vitest checks each emulator theme field against the light and the dark `:root` of `tokens.css` and computes each ANSI colour's contrast in both schemes; in the browser harness (U26), under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, `.xterm-viewport`'s computed background is the colour the dark `--ground` resolves to. Test: `u59_`.
rules.cases: Rule (widen): any colour the App paints, whether through a stylesheet or a JS option object (xterm `ITheme`, canvas), is the value of a Token in the active scheme, and a scheme change repaints it. Cases: (1) Terminal background in dark. Wrong: #ffffff, a white block in a dark pane. Right: dark `--ground`. (2) Terminal foreground and cursor in dark. Wrong: #1d1d1f on dark. Right: dark `--text`. (3) Selection in dark. Wrong: rgba(0,0,0,.05), invisible on dark. Right: dark `--selected`. (4) ANSI `black` (#1d1d1f) in dark. Wrong: unreadable on the dark ground. Right: a dark-palette entry at 4.5:1. Probes: the user switches the scheme with a Terminal open → it repaints without a reload; prefers-contrast: more → foreground stays `--text`; a program sets its own background → it is drawn as asked (exception kept); the WebGL renderer → the same theme fields; the U83 earlier-run snapshot → follows the scheme; the empty-Terminal notch (U55) → uses Tokens; the PadDrawer → already Tokens via CSS; the Rail Glyphs → CSS Tokens, unaffected; light scheme → the existing light palette, unchanged; reduced motion → no repaint animation. Counterexample hunted: a program's own truecolour background. Narrowed by keeping U59's 'drawn as it asks' exception.
